title: Polyclinic waiting times for walk-in patients and plans to spread patient load
asked: Mr Vikram Nair asked what the average waiting times at polyclinics are for walk-in patients during peak and off-peak hours, and whether there are plans to redistribute patient load across off-peak hours.
response: Dr Koh Poh Koon said that in 2025 the median and 95th percentile doctor consultation waiting times for walk-in patients were eight minutes and 72 minutes, and that MOH does not track waiting times by peak versus off-peak hours. He said clinics schedule fewer appointments than full capacity to leave room for walk-in patients with acute medical needs, and that scheduled appointments had a median wait of about 10 minutes and a 95th percentile of up to 52 minutes in 2025. He described how complex cases can push back patients seen later in a session, and said walk-in patients triaged as non-urgent may be given an appointment for the next day. He also pointed to CHAS-subsidised GP clinics and Healthier SG enrolment as ways to spread load beyond polyclinics.
